summary: Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine and Walter Eugene Clark, and under Kalipada Tarkacharya. He held a junior fellowship and later professorships at Harvard (circa 1958–1999).

Daniel John Gogerly was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (circa 1818–1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as an officer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (circa 1845–1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer worked in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Westmar, Garrett-Evangelical, and the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn, Mircea Eliade, and Joseph M. Kitagawa. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (circa 1973–2001).

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, mentored by Alexander von Rospatt among other teachers. In 2017, he held an assistant professorship at the University of South Carolina.

Daniel M. Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University in 1999, and held a post at California State University, Chico (attested 2006).
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ngawang Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1980 to 2022.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his thesis at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel S. Capper is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, where he studied under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Schlumberger worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1923–1925) and held a post at Princeton University (circa 1956–1958).

Daniel Sperber is a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Kol Torah, Kilburn Grammar School, Yeshivah of Flatbush, and University College London (circa 1963–1968), and held posts at Bar-Ilan University (circa 1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jay L. Garfield and studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held instructor posts at the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.
Daniela Berti is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Siena. She held a fellowship at the Centre d'Etudes Himalayennes (attested 2004).

Daniela Bevilacqua is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Danielle Feller is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2001 under Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.

Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot in the 1930s, later serving as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (circa 1952–1992).

Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi, Jai Narain Vyas University, and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (circa 1970–1973).

Daud Ali is a historian and Indologist. He earned his BA at William & Mary and his MA and PhD at the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught at SOAS (circa 1994–2008) before joining the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

Dave Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019), studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.
David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and held a post at Stony Brook University around 1970.
